title: ChatGPT's Capabilities in Spotting and Analyzing Writing Errors Experienced by EFL Learners
venue: Arab World English Journal (AWEJ) Special Issue on CALL Number 9
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT can effectively detect and analyze writing errors made by EFL learners, and how its performance compares with human instructors. The core problem addressed is the potential of large language models to support writing feedback, while recognizing that such tools may struggle with deeper aspects of language use such as pragmatics and discourse-level meaning.

The authors used ChatGPT and human instructor analysis on the same student writing samples. The study was corpus-based and mixed-methods: quantitative analysis was used to count and classify error types, while qualitative analysis was used to interpret the nature and sources of errors. The paper reports that ChatGPT was able to identify many surface-level issues such as grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization, and sentence structure, and it could also generate revised versions of text.

The participants were university students from two departments at Taiz University in Yemen: English Department students and Computer Science Department students enrolled in writing-related courses. The paper concludes that ChatGPT is useful for identifying surface errors and supporting writing analysis, but it does not replace human teachers, who were better at identifying deep-structure and pragmatic problems. The authors argue that combining AI tools with teacher expertise may provide the most effective feedback for EFL writing instruction.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed mixed-methods descriptive comparison, but it is not a randomized controlled trial and provides limited methodological detail beyond error counts and an ANOVA. The evidence is therefore informative but only moderately credible for causal claims.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests useful support for surface-level writing feedback, but the findings are mixed and the paper does not report a clear effect size showing meaningful improvement over human instruction. The practical impact appears modest and limited to specific writing-error detection tasks.

interventions.use_case: using ChatGPT to analyze EFL student writing, identify errors, and generate feedback/revisions for teachers and learners
automated error detection and revision suggestions for student writing, focused on grammar, spelling, punctuation, sentence structure, and clarity
ChatGPT as an AI-assisted writing analysis tool for EFL error spotting, style analysis, and proofreading support

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT identified most surface-level writing errors in EFL texts and provided useful revision suggestions, but it failed to detect many deep-structure and pragmatics-related errors that human instructors noticed. The paper reports descriptive comparisons and an ANOVA on error-type frequencies (F=1.500472, p=0.230426), but does not provide a standardized effect size for the teacher-vs-ChatGPT accuracy difference.
finding.measure: Writing error detection and classification in EFL student paragraphs; comparison of detected error frequencies by ChatGPT versus human instructors

finding.finding_summary: As a writing support tool, ChatGPT produced coherent revised versions of student paragraphs and offered proofreading, sentence rephrasing, and style suggestions. Its strongest performance was on surface-level literacy features such as grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization, and sentence structure, but this was not sufficient for full replacement of human feedback.
finding.measure: Quality of AI-generated writing feedback, proofreading, and revised text suggestions
